occurrence: Title of Trystan S. Goetze’s paper “AI Art is Theft: Labour, Extraction, and Exploitation” (arXiv, version 2; first posted January 2024), which argues that image generators involve labour theft from artists.

P1.reason: “Theft” states wrongdoing as settled. As a moral argument about consent and pay, it is a position people can debate; as a statement of fact, US courts have not established it, and one court found a specific training use fair.

P2.reason: Read as the paper's argument, “theft” is about training on artists' work without consent or pay, not about every image being a copy. That applies broadly: Midjourney's founder said in 2022 that it did not seek consent from living artists for its training images. (Rescored October 7, 2026 at Leyla's request; was N for treating copying as universal.)

W1.reason: “Theft” is a crime word. It adds force beyond the supported point, that artists' work was used without consent or pay. This is distinct from P1, which scores stating a contested legal and moral judgment as settled. (Rescored October 7, 2026; was Y.)

W2.reason: No human-like agency is attributed to AI.

review_status: AI research draft; not independently reviewed
